name: OM-89
question: Does oral OM-89 reduce recurrent urinary tract infections in women compared with placebo over 12 months?

design.population: 454 ambulatory women aged 18–65 years with at least three documented UTIs in the preceding year, acute UTI symptoms for at least two days, and bacteriuria of at least 10³/mL were randomized; 453 received treatment and entered the ITT analysis. A post-baseline acute UTI required at least one week without anti-infectives, at least 10³ bacteria/mL in urine, and at least two of dysuria, frequency, and burning on urination for at least two days.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 543; Results, p 544

verdictNote: All three prespecified primary efficacy endpoints favored OM-89 in the ITT analysis.
takeaway: In 453 treated women with recurrent UTI, oral OM-89 reduced mean post-baseline UTIs over 12 months versus placebo (0.84 vs 1.28; placebo-minus-OM-89 difference 0.44, 95% CI 0.15–0.73; p = 0.0026); both other prespecified primary endpoints also favored OM-89.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Bauer HW, Alloussi S, Egger G, Blümlein HM, Cozma G, Schulman CC. "A long-term, multicenter, double-blind study of an Escherichia coli extract (OM-89) in female patients with recurrent urinary tract infections." *Eur Urol.* 2005;47(4):542-548. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2004.12.009

results.measure: Mean post-baseline UTI episodes per woman over 12 months (ITT); effect is placebo minus OM-89
results.note: The paper reports an unweighted placebo-minus-OM-89 effect of 0.44 (95% confidence limits 0.15–0.73), corresponding to a 34% lower relapse rate.

results.endpoint: Women with at least one post-baseline UTI
results.measure: Women with at least one post-baseline UTI over 12 months (ITT); risk difference in percentage points
results.note: The paper reports a 14.7-point reduction and odds ratio 0.55. Its printed 95% CI for the difference (−23.8 to 5.6 points) is discordant with p = 0.001; the interval is transcribed as printed.

results.endpoint: Distribution of post-baseline UTI recurrences per woman
results.measure: Number of post-baseline UTI recurrences per woman over 12 months (ITT)
results.note: Mann–Whitney test for the full distribution; 185 versus 276 total post-baseline episodes. Table 3 includes missing recurrence data for 11 and 7 women.

results.measure: Mean number of anti-infective prescriptions during follow-up; analysis-set denominators not specified
results.note: Secondary efficacy measures were analyzed descriptively for exploratory interpretation; prescriptions included anti-infectives for reasons other than UTI.
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Statistical methods, p 543; Results, p 545

results.endpoint: Post-baseline UTI episodes by study interval
results.measure: Observed episodes in months 1–6 and months 7–12 (ITT)

values.exp: 99 episodes in months 1–6; 86 in months 7–12 (n = 231 ITT)
values.ctl: 125 episodes in months 1–6; 151 in months 7–12 (n = 222 ITT)

results.note: The study was not designed to quantify the booster courses' contribution to the treatment effect.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 545; Discussion, p 547

harms.label: Serious adverse events

values.exp: 11 events (n = 231 treated; number of affected patients not reported)
values.ctl: 4 events (n = 222 treated; number of affected patients not reported)

harms.note: Investigators assessed none of the serious adverse events as related to study medication; most were hospitalizations for sequelae of pre-existing disease.

delivery.label: Oral treatment schedule

values.exp: One capsule containing 6 mg lyophilized E. coli lysate daily for 90 days, then the first 10 days of months 7, 8, and 9
values.ctl: One matching placebo capsule on the same schedule

delivery.note: No study capsule was given during months 4–6 or 10–12.

delivery.label: Adherence assessment
delivery.value: Compliance was checked by returned blister packs; per-protocol analysis required at least 70% compliance and data from all six visits. Actual adherence rates were not reported.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Statistical methods, p 543
